lock_files.notes: Same flock(2) lease files as any-core.sh, both-cores.sh and pf-launch. Lock order: GPU files first (testing-gpu.lock, then testing-gpu-<UUID>.lock), then core leases. Owner job units take them for their lifetime (GPU files handed over by the queue's GPU claim when the GPU was contended); the worker itself only observes /proc/locks. Borrow jobs hold borrow-core<K>.lock shared instead, never the core lease; holding borrow-core<K>.lock exclusively from outside the queue marks core K as not lendable.

borrow.notes: Borrow jobs (simq submit --borrow) run in simqborrow.slice, a top-level slice of the user manager with cpu.idle=1, as units with CPUWeight=1, SCHED_IDLE and idle I/O class: every owner job unit and every process of the terminal sessions wins the CPU. A lease holder or owner job is idle when its process tree used at most idle_threshold cores above a whole number over idle_window_s and the core itself was at most cpu_idle_threshold busy; a borrower lent such a core is preempted when the tree uses more than the cores left to it plus busy_threshold over busy_window_s. A frozen borrower is requeued after freeze_max_s or shortly before its time limit.

notes: Each partition names physical cores by their lowest logical CPU (0-7); SMT siblings 8-15 are never allocated.
memory_schedulable is the sum of --mem over concurrent jobs (31 GiB RAM; about 3 GiB left for the system).
The GPU is shared by raikou-mfem and powerflow: exclusive per job unless --gpu-mem is given and the 11G budget allows sharing.

Lending (0.6.1): every partition lends its free cores and the idle cores of its running jobs to borrow jobs (lend: true). Cores leased by tools outside the queue (any-core.sh, both-cores.sh, pf-launch) are not lent (lend_leased_idle: false): such holders have no time limit and no way to mark timing runs.

powerflow is not timing_sensitive as a partition: timing-sensitive Power-Flow runs submit with --exclusive-timing, which keeps the job's cores and their SMT siblings unlent while it runs, and its other core stays usable by borrow jobs. Set timing_sensitive: true on a partition to keep borrow jobs off all of its cores and siblings, including its own borrow jobs.
No GPU is ever lent: borrow jobs cannot request GPUs.

gpu_line.notes: 0.6.2 GPU line. Queued GPU jobs that are ready except for the GPU join the line through a claim unit (<prefix>-gpuclaim-<token>.service) that waits for testing-gpu.lock in the kernel queue, then takes testing-gpu-<UUID>.lock, and hands both open files to the job unit (SCM_RIGHTS), so the lock is never released in between and the job's time limit starts with its unit. gpu-lease users publish tickets in ticket_dir; members are served by since-time (a claim's is the submit time of its oldest ready job, a helper's its start time). Processes blocked in a raw flock on the GPU files (command in requeue_commands, not a job-control job of an interactive shell) are moved behind the line with SIGSTOP+SIGCONT; every move is logged in log_path. state_path lists the waiting queue jobs with their since-times, the claim, the holders and the raw waiters (heartbeat every 10 s; stale after stale_after_s, withdrawn when the worker stops). A held claim that no job takes within claim_hold_max_s releases the GPU.
